expectations: remembering the person server in the browser
context: constraint: constitution 3.0.0 Principles I, II, IV, VII
intent: Sign in to Umbral with a Mastodon-compatible fediverse account through a built-in Fediverse connector

decisions.decision: Support = OAuth metadata with S256 and app_registration_endpoint, or NodeInfo software gotosocial
decisions.why: PKCE is required; GoToSocial enforces S256 without metadata
decisions.rejected: Send PKCE to every server (Akkoma/Pleroma ignore it silently)

decisions.decision: Fediverse beside the adapters, not an IProviderAdapter
decisions.why: per-server client chosen at run time

decisions.decision: Second HttpClient umbral-fediverse with connect-time public-address guard
decisions.why: only check DNS cannot dodge; keeps LAN OIDC providers working
decisions.rejected: Guard on the shared umbral-provider client

decisions.decision: Per-server secrets always in the local Data Protection key ring
decisions.why: created by Umbral, one per server

decisions.decision: Client-credentials check before redirect when not checked in 24h; re-register once on invalid_client
decisions.why: Mastodon shows its own error for an unknown client and never redirects back

decisions.decision: Allowlist checks typed domain before contact and the WebFinger-resolved server after
decisions.why: FR-009 no contact with unlisted servers

plan.summary: Plan, research R1-R14, data model (schema v7) and routes contract for the Fediverse connector
plan.key_finding: Akkoma and Pleroma have no PKCE, GoToSocial has PKCE but no metadata

approach: A Fediverse module beside the provider adapters: pure parsing in Domains/Fediverse.fs, a registration store, an SSRF-guarded HTTP client, an account-step handler and callback sharing Callback.fs's sign-in tail, and a Connectors pane. Correlation cookie carries the server; schema v7 adds fediverse_servers and profile columns.
